hero: In a pediatric oncology ward of a Manila government hospital, a Filipino pediatric nephrologist and a female oncology fellow study an ECG strip beside the bed of a 6-year-old Filipino boy with a chemotherapy line, while his mother sits holding his hand; cardiac monitor glowing, focused and caring mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Tumor lysis releases potassium, phosphate and uric acid that threaten heart and kidney.
figures.content: Left: tumor cells bursting, arrows labeled 'Potassium', 'Phosphate', 'Nucleic acids'. Center: nucleic acids to 'Uric acid'; kidney tubule cross-section with crystals labeled 'Uric acid crystals' and 'Calcium phosphate'. Right top: heart with ECG peaked T wave labeled 'K ≥6.0 mmol/L'. Right bottom: calcium gauge low labeled 'Ca ≤1.75 mmol/L'. Bottom banner: 'Lab TLS: 2 or more within 3 days before to 7 days after therapy'.

figures.teaches: Hyperkalemia treatment in a child follows stabilize, shift, remove.
figures.content: Top box 'High potassium' then decision 'Real or artifact?' (repeat free-flowing sample). Then 'ECG changed?' yes arrow to 'Stabilize: calcium'. Then 'Shift: insulin + dextrose, beta-2 agonist'. Then 'Remove: diuretic, binder, dialysis'. Then 'Recheck K and glucose at set time'. Side note box: 'Doses from pediatric formulary; read back weight'.

card: An ECG strip and a pediatric chemotherapy bag beside a child's hospital bed, no text.
